data.name: Agni
data.gender_notes: Agni is used as a masculine name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Agni is the Hindu God of Fire. He is responsible for the creation, preservation, and destruction of the universe. Agni is also believed to be the bridge between the physical and spiritual worlds, and the source of all life energy. The name Agni carries the meaning “Fire God” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Agni usually hope their child will grow to embody fire god and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of transformation, purification, and sacrifice.
data.etymology: Agni belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Fire God.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Agni total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: Agni is an essential deity in Hinduism and holds a significant place in various Hindu rituals. Fire is an essential element for many Hindus, and Agni is regarded as the god of the fire, which holds great importance in their daily life. Agni is invoked during rituals like yajna (sacred fires), vivah (marriage) and cremation ceremonies. Agni is also a significant element in the Hindu tradition of deep-rooted hospitality. Fire is often lit in front of temples and homes to represent the divine presence and to ward off negative energies. Agni is also believed to purify and sanctify the offerings made during rituals.
data.spiritual_significance: Agni is believed to bridge the physical and spiritual worlds in Hinduism. He represents the purifying, illuminating, and transformative aspects of fire. Fire is the source of all life energy and is revered for its ability to consume, purify, and transform opposition into ashes. Agni is the deity of the cosmic energy present in fire, which is considered the link between the material and immaterial aspects of the universe. Agni is also believed to be the soul of the universe, as it is present everywhere, burning continuously and sustaining all life forms. Agni is also considered to be the messenger of the gods and is invoked to carry our prayers and offerings to the deities.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Agni, the Hindu deity of fire, represents the transformative power of consciousness. It is the purifier, the illuminator, and the transcendental bridge between the physical and spiritual realms. Through Agni's fiery touch, we are consumed and purified, emerging renewed and reborn.

historical_references.reference: Agni is a Hindu deity, often referred to as the god of fire. He is mentioned in the Rigveda, an ancient Indian scripture, as one of the main deities. Agni is invoked at the beginning of every Vedic fire ritual to create and maintain the sacred fire. His role is crucial in various rituals, including the sacrificial fire.

Agni is also associated with the mythological fire from the churning of the ocean (Samudra Manthan) in Hindu mythology. The gods and demons joined forces to churn the ocean to obtain the elixir of immortality, Amrita. Agni was the divine serpent who held the churning rod in his mouth and agitated the ocean.

trends: Fire in Hinduism is considered a symbol of purity, knowledge and power. It is also the god of the Agnihotra ritual, which is still practiced today in some Hindu households.
Fire is used extensively in various Hindu rituals and ceremonies such as weddings, funerals, and festivals like Diwali and Holi.
